annotations.text:
All of this lands in one file: src/index.css.

The @theme block plus the :root and .dark blocks are the whole change. Component markup stays as it is — 4,254 utility usages already read from these tokens.

The rail is the exception: that one is a shell rewrite.

Rail spec at the bottom of this sheet.

It carries labels rather than icons alone — a full-timer has 13 destinations and the reference product has 6. That also retires the More menu, since PRIMARY_BY_ROLE only ever promoted 3.

The icon-only version is kept beside it as the dropped alternative.

Real screens, real copy, real component dimensions — lifted from MyDay.tsx, TopNav.tsx and index.css rather than invented.

The Journey board is here because it is the hardest case: its stage colours are persisted in Firestore as class names, so they survive the switch and become the only colour on screen.

Same page, same content, same tokens — only the shell differs.

The rail costs 132px of content width (10%) and buys back the More menu, which currently hides ten of a full-timer's thirteen destinations.

Three shells behind one stored preference, following the shape ThemeProvider already set.

Two findings worth reading: the expanded rail does not fit a 13" laptop and has to scroll inside itself, and the 1024–1279 forced collapse must not write back to storage.
